Team —

Quick context: Exec leadership asked us to identify ~20% run-rate savings across our CS stack by removing overlapping seats and consolidating workflows between Intercom (messaging + inbox) and Gainsight (customer success playbooks + timelines). Goal is to reduce duplicate licenses for CS reps and centralize routing to the Intercom inbox where possible, while keeping Gainsight for health/renewals automation.

Ask: can you each take the vendor side you own and confirm the following by EOD Friday?
- Current seat counts and renewal dates (per SKU)
- Any hard limits that would prevent moving historical conversation data into Intercom (retention, export formats)
- Short list of contract exceptions we need (SLA, data residency, seat swap mechanics)

Marissa — you own vendor conversations. Stephanie — coordinate with Ops for migration effort estimate. Lauren — I’ll loop legal once we have quotes and SOWs.

I’ll run a quick sync with vendors next week; please flag any blockers.

Thanks,

Rishi — quick notes from calls this week (Sara @ Intercom and Ben @ Gainsight). Summary bullets: 

Intercom (Sara Liu)
- Intercom can consolidate our inbox and messaging into an Enterprise plan; they counted 85 active CS seats today.
- Offered 18% consolidation discount if we commit to a 24-month seat minimum for 70 seats.
- Data migration: they support conversation exports via JSON/CSV and offer a paid migration service (estimate: 2–3 weeks for our volume).
- Attachment: preliminary quote expected Friday (Sara said shes sending a PDF).

Gainsight (Ben Howard)
- Gainsight proposes reducing seat counts from 60 -> 30 for seat-based features; licensing for Playbooks and Rules will remain at account-level.
- SOW outlines a customization window for health score mappings — they require an engineering kickoff for two weeks of mapping work.
- Risks: removing CS inbox from Gainsight will break a couple of legacy automations (we can rebuild in Intercom but need backlog & timeline).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Get Intercom quote and migration SOW (Sara).
2) Get Gainsight final SOW with exact seat counts and mapping estimate (Ben).
3) Legal to review both and mark contract exceptions we need.

I can run a vendor consolidation call next Thurs 1pm PT if that works for people.

—Marissa

Rishi / Team —

Thanks for the packet. Legal has reviewed the quotes and SOW and we can make the following concessions to keep timeline and pricing intact: 

1) EU data residency: we can accept Intercoms regioning clause provided they sign a standard Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and we add a limited representation specific to EU data handling.
2) Seat swap mechanics: approve a mid-term seat reallocation clause where Redwood can move up to 15% of seats between CS products once per 12-month period; require 30 days written notice and vendor confirmation of license changes.

Conditions: Both concessions require (a) vendors to sign the final DocuSign agreements with the redlines in Legal_Redlines_20260710.pdf and (b) a joint migration runbook between Intercom, Gainsight, and SupportConsulting.

Next steps I recommend: 
- Rishi: send updated acceptance email to Sara + Ben and ask them to prepare final DocuSign packages reflecting redlines.
- Marissa: coordinate a kickoff with Javier for migration runbook and engineering dates.
- Stephanie: prepare a resource plan for the two sprints Ben referenced.

Once DocuSign is live well route to Finance for PO and billing setup.

Lauren Bishop
